newsitem.title: INDIA: India extends jute packaging requirement for 2 yrs.
newsitem.headline: India extends jute packaging requirement for 2 yrs.

text.p: The Indian government has extended a law requiring the foodgrains, sugar and fertiliser industries to use jute in packaging, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency said late on Sunday that the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs extended the 1987 law for two years.
PTI said the foodgrains and sugar industries would have to continue using only jute in its packaging, while the fertiliser sector would have to use at least 50 percent jute.
Sugar for export or in small consumer packs of five kg or less would be exempt from the requirement, PTI said.
The Business Line newspaper said the cabinet committee deferred a decision on the packaging of cement in jute bags.
PTI said cement plants with a daily production capacity of 100 tonnes or less would be exempt from the law. It gave no information regarding bigger plants.

It said the cabinet committee set the minimum support price for TD-5 grade jute in Assam state at 570 rupees per quintal for the 1997-98 season. The minimum support price for other varieties and grades of raw jute would be fixed in light of normal market price differentials.
The news agency gave no other details.
